questions.question: In a certain code language, 'POSITIVE' is written as '109' and 'NEGATIVE' is written as '141'. How will 'INTEGER' be written in that language?
questions.solution:
The table is alphabets place value:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/889ff2be8a048327f450a975a401b2f4241e5f28d86896613386ad4014cb4505.png] 

The pattern followed here;

Sum of the opposite alphabets place value + Number of letters in the word = Number

POSITIVE is coded as 109 →

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3b2da6035e4075629eda2e482116511bab020becfe517f67a6806a62637cee5c.png] 

→ (11 + 12 + 8 + 18 + 7 + 18 + 5 + 22) + 8 = 101 + 8 = 109

And,

NEGATIVE is coded as 141 →

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4a1e1828fdf7ed086cc4f30b741a458d8fc8a824e5a1f19dd2c463bfb40aa355.png] 

(13 + 22 + 20 + 26 + 7 + 18 + 5 +22) + 8 = 141

Similarly,

INTEGER is coded as ? →

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7584654edc654ed960ff2a93cfcc94b658416c1558f0fb96adbec5e416501010.png] 

(18 + 13 + 7 + 22 + 20 + 22 + 9) + 7 =118

Hence, the correct answer is "118".

questions.question:
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation.

(31 * 3 ) * 64 * 124 * (492 * 78) * 6
questions.solution:
Here, we use the table given below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/54b4ff1ba6fe0e9a55606f49f4df2602e9af65194f8960f44baeb26e044c3e00.png] 

1) +, ÷, −, =, −, × →

Given equation: (31 * 3) * 64 * 124 * (492 * 78) * 6 

After replacing the * by the symbols in the given option and using the BODMAS rule,

we get:

(31 + 3) ÷ 64 - 124 = (492 - 78) × 6

⇒ 34 ÷ 64 - 124 = 414 × 6

⇒ 34 ÷ 64 - 124 = 2484

⇒ 34 ÷ 64 - 124 = 2484

⇒ - 123.46 ≠ 2484

2) −, ×, =, −, −, ÷ →

Given equation: (31 * 3) * 64 * 124 * (492 * 78) * 6 

After replacing the * by the symbols in the given option and using the BODMAS rule,

we get:

(31 - 3) × 64 = 124 - (492 - 78) ÷ 6 

⇒ 28 × 64 = 124 - 414 ÷ 6

⇒ 1792 = 124 - 69

⇒ 1792 ≠ 55

3) +, −, +, ÷, ×, = →

Given equation: (31 * 3) * 64 * 124 * (492 * 78) * 6 

After replacing the * by the symbols in the given option and using the BODMAS rule,

we get:

(31 + 3) - 64 + 124 ÷ (492 × 78) = 6 

⇒ 34 - 64 + 124 ÷ 38376 = 6

⇒ -30 + 124 ÷ 38376 ≠ 6 

4) ×, −, =, −, +, ÷ →

Given equation: (31 * 3) * 64 * 124 * (492 * 78) * 6 

After replacing the * by the symbols in the given option and using the BODMAS rule,

we get:

(31 × 3) - 64 = 124 - (492 + 78) ÷ 6 

⇒ 93 - 64 = 124 - 570 ÷ 6

⇒ 29 = 124 - 95

⇒ 29 = 29

 Hence the correct answer is "×, −, =, −, +, ÷"

questions.question:
'A # B' means 'A is the husband of B'

'A @ B' means 'A is the son of B'

'A & B' means 'A is the mother of B'

'A % B' means 'A is the paternal grandfather of B'

If 'K % N @ P # R', then how is K related to R?
questions.solution:
The following Family tree is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71c77462ffae048bd2427f8683c47f070790a6a1de0f7523bd5b01ae35f93635.png] 

 
 

 
 
A is

 
 
 

 
 
Symbol

 
 
 
#

 
 
 
@

 
 
 
&

 
 
 
%

 
 
 

 
 
Meaning

 
 
 
Husband

 
 
 
Son

 
 
 
Mother

 
 
 
Paternal grandfather

 
 
 

 
 
Of B

 
 
 

 

 

 

 

 

1) K % N → K is paternal grandfather of N.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ecbb5c60393fa88a2365c05679088f6a405f170e7cab0fb2e52399e59d4eda44.png] 

 

2) N @ P → N is the son of P.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4969742861dfbd6da7e2c1c47dd1b2f5f209a507d1f80905926cf16a4319e6a8.png] 

3) P # R → P is the husband of R.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d90a11c29fe052a773efa0d596e70590cdef6420a0b4d87f4b8f02cbb0ca2d07.png] 

So the final family tree is as follows:

K % N @ P # R

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eee24284d88d6a164ac0635181821719ef9c28b3dc1bc4c51b39164a51321e6f.png] 

K is father in law of R.

Hence, the Correct answer is "Father-in-law".

questions.question:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

306 ÷ 17 + 4 - 50 × 8 = 30
questions.solution:
__BODMAS Rule:__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7751840ca1840d12cadc428f84d30e2cdcd5e7f82d52a57de21f2404c58eed88.png] 

Option 1) + and -

After interchanging the sign we get:

⇒ __306 ÷ 17__ - 4 + 50 × 8 = 30

⇒ 18 - 4 +__ 50 × 8 __= 30

⇒ __18__ - 4 __+ 400__ = 30

⇒ 418 - 4 = 30

⇒ 414 ≠ 30

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) ÷ and ×

After interchanging the sign we get:

⇒ 306 × 17 + 4 - __50 ÷ 8 __= 30

⇒ __306 × 17 __+ 4 - 6.25 = 30

⇒ __5205 + 4 __- 6.25 = 30

⇒__ 5209 - 6.25__ = 30

⇒ 5202.75 ≠ 30

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) × and -

After interchanging the sign we get:

⇒ __306 ÷ 17__ + 4 × 50 - 8 = 30

⇒ 18 + __4 × 50__ - 8 = 30

⇒ __18 + 200__ - 8 = 30

⇒ __218 - 8__ = 30

⇒ 210 ≠ 30

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) + and × 

After interchanging the sign we get:

⇒ __306 ÷ 17__ × 4 - 50 + 8 = 30

⇒ __18 × 4__ - 50 + 8 = 30

⇒ __72 __- 50 __+ 8__ = 30

⇒ __80 - 50__ = 30

⇒ 30 = 30

⇒ LHS = RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

questions.question: There are five friends, Ankita, Parul, Ashna, Bhanu, Ritika. Ashna is the tallest. Ankita is shorter than Parul but taller than Ritika. Bhanu is shorter than Parul but taller than Ankita. Who is taller than Ritika but shorter than Bhanu?
questions.solution:
Given

1) Ashna is the tallest.

2) Ankita is shorter than Parul but taller than Ritika.

Parul > Ankita > Ritika

3) Bhanu is shorter than Parul but taller than Ankita.

Parul > Bhanu > Ankita

Combing all (1), (2) and (3) we get

Ashna > Parul > Bhanu > Ankita > Ritika

Hence, the correct answer is "Ankita".

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'RAID' is written as 'DIARS' and 'SPOT' is written as 'TOPST'. How will 'MOOT' be written in that language?

 [IMAGE: https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/7gEdodjoBc_Hsj7j8b7Nf3s6o8dMs-ylY7Gt0xAFH6KJsh_ixFoOBrU32C30Zp10-FB177zeQZO959ifwwm3uhwZOA-j49sE6eL56-gbPqqriVHiqNM90Fz8hu-fKiph7vPjaPc4r1XXxEoCiC44isJX0tdYAiyJXP3dv1JyVd_u7GYBOrmXj7sGyyH1] 

In each word, the letters are first Reversed from right to left and then one is added to the place value of the 4th letter of the newly formed word to get the 5th letter of the newly formed word.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50940743eca303448d2daa522502db627656a34b0ce2d68ae0da9c9423c99f29.png] 

Hence, the correct answer is "TOOMN".

questions.question: Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are sitting in a straight row, facing the north. Only two people sit to the right of D. Only two people sit to the left of C. Only two people sit between D and G. Only three people sit between C and E. A is not an immediate neighbour of D. B sits to the right of D. Who sits at the centre?
questions.solution:
Given, Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a row facing north.

1) Only two people sit to the right of D and Only two people sit to the left of C.

Thus D will be third from the right end and C will be third from the left end.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/81eba0e38e80de9416713e693211a5b4b78c3c25da2fdbd5a25f20781aecaf86.png] 

2) Only two people sit between D and G, then it is only possible when G will be to the left of D.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/228344b2e12498bbc062d62fcc0da620b15953ab2baa4e9af241bdc67a1c2894.png] 

3) Only three people sit between C and E, then it is only possible when E will be to the right of C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c0d1ee1e9ce44f605c0bfdc85e1ad3bd31044f83c288375fadf66c88ed3ef14.png] 

4) A is not an immediate neighbour of D, then there is only one place left for A, i.e. extreme left of the row.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/599358d9c5c8b571938ba5274ae56971c83c0d5de7a466f36593b0cabfb42b45.png] 

5) B sits to the right of D, then B will take only space left between D and E.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/13cc52c1b4db4ba7f9112dca4c8573a7e14d390444b4cae4a9ccf47b18260b9f.png] 

6) Now there is only one space left and it will be taken by F.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35cd9e4d6033138382c1faec9d9a71fc30f02a14b5eff94a3b9680f81d8a5685.png] 

Hence, the correct answer is "F".

questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some cushions are sofas.

Some purses are cushions.

All sofas are purses.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some cushions are purses.

II. Some purses are sofas.

III. Some sofas are cushions.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram is,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77cf3c9fdb50200264abb91bec4b06e933df42cc7b47ecc3809e33149ddac3d4.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some cushions are purses → Follows (As some purses are cushions, then some cushions will also be purses).

II. Some purses are sofas → Follows (As all sofas are purses, then some purses will be sofas).

III. Some sofas are cushions → Follows (As some cushions are sofas, then some sofas will be cushions).

Hence, the correct answer is "All conclusions follow".
